gate_claims.claim: cocotb is a backend of simulator.run chosen by backend: cocotb, and without that name the backend refuses to run
a simulator.run without backend still means an HDL testbench (cocotb is registered after the HDL backends)
the backend refuses unless named, so the run records backend: cocotb
the backend requires sources, top and cocotb
simulator.run takes sources, top, expect and the cocotb parameter in the tool catalog
expect takes pass or no value, any other value is refused and nothing runs
a test file must be a .py file named as a Python module and two files may not share a name, refused before anything runs
two test modules with the same name are refused
tests it cannot judge (expect other than pass, bad file names, duplicate names) are refused
with cocotb every HDL source is design: one that ends the simulation, reads arguments, opens a file or reaches outside the language is refused
HDL that could stand in for the verdict is refused (each listed construct and token pasting)
the run passes only when cocotb wrote its results file
at least one test passed
a failed test fails the run, with the failing test's assertion text in the summary
the totals line must be printed exactly once
the totals line must agree with the results file
the steps must exit zero, and passing results with a nonzero exit still fail
exit status alone is not read: a run with no results file fails whatever the exit status
a totals line printed by the design can only fail the run
a run made with this backend answers a requirement only when the requirement fixes backend: cocotb
cocotb is the one verdict backend, so it never stands in for an HDL testbench's verdict gate
a cocotb pass never meets a gate for an HDL testbench's verdict
cocotb counts tests, not checks, so a test that asserts nothing passes
the Python is not sandboxed and could write a passing results file itself (the test modules are copied and run under vvp with no sandbox or filter)
the must-fail scorer runs the same tests on a planted mutant of the RTL and requires them to fail
the tests must fail each broken counter (must-fail on cocotb tests)
the timeout stops a Python test that never returns (the document's advice to bound a test)
